messages:
ava: paging: multiple Xid 13/31 bursts on gpu-rack-3/node-04 and node-05 since ~03:12 UTC; seeing container exits and OOMKilled on a few tenant jobs. tagging oncall.
infra-bot: Incident created (INC-2026-058) · severity: P1 · notified: @oncall. Logs collected: /var/log/inc/5071239999.tar.gz
ricardo: dashboards show sudden spike in ECC correctable errors on both GPUs in node-04; driver reset events correlating with spikes. Some pods show `OOMKilled` right after driver reset.
tay: customer impact? which routes/tenants?
ava: tenant-b and internal-test-suite saw failures; tenant-b route /v1/chat had ~18% 500s over last 9m.
oncall-bot: oncall ack: @tay taking.
tay: running quick checks: `ssh gpu-node-04 -- sudo dmesg | tail -n 60` shows repeated `NVRM: Xid (13):` and `EDAC MC0: CE` lines. Also `journalctl -u nvidia-driver -n 200` has driver restarts.
emily: kube: pods on node-04 show CrashLoopBackOff; `kubectl get events -n tenant-b` has `OOMKilled` and `ContainerCannotStart` intermittent.
ricardo: `nvidia-smi -q` shows ECC Corrected: 312, GPU Reset Count: 7 for GPU0. PCIe errors present.
tay: mitigation plan: 1) mark both nodes unschedulable 2) incrementally evacuate non-critical pods 3) move live traffic to hotspare pool 4) start hardware diag with hw-team if resets persist after drain.
ava: will cordon now: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-04` -> done. starting `kubectl drain` with `--pod-selector='priority!=critical'` to avoid evicting critical serving pods.
infra-bot: Warning: cluster autoscaler may trigger scale-up due to drain. Temporarily set cluster-autoscaler:scale-down=false.
ricardo: please avoid mass rescheduling to single spare — use `spread-scheduler` hints.
emily: invoking graceful eviction for critical pods: checkpointing state then evict with 120s grace.
tay: after partial drain, two critical pods remained pinned to node-04 (stateful inference). I'm initiating live checkpoint copy to S3 then will evict.
ava: checkpoint complete for those two. evicting now.
oncall-bot: customer comm required? tenant-b SLA impacts >10% for 10m. Recommend sending bridge.
emily: opening customer bridge and posting status update to tenant-b support channel.
infra-bot: Action: redirect 100% tenant-b /v1/chat traffic from dedicated-pool-east -> fallback-gpu-pool-west via route switch API.
ricardo: route switch in flight; capacity check: fallback-gpu-pool-west now at 72% util.
tay: after traffic shift error rate dropped to ~6%. Good. Continue monitoring 15m.
ava: attempted `systemctl restart nvidia-driver` on node-04 after draining -> driver came up but Xid resumed immediately (~30s after restart).
emily: persistent immediate Xids after driver reload usually point to hardware ECC/chip issue or bad power/thermals.
ricardo: agree. We'll isolate hardware. scheduling hardware ticket HT-8892 and flagging node-04 for removal from rotation.
tay: plan: set node-04 label `hardware:needs-replace` and keep cordoned. Recreate workloads on healthy nodes.
ava: applied label and posted to ops-inventory.
infra-bot: Notice: spare capacity dipping to 85% after reschedules. Manual intervention may be required if further quarantines occur.
emily: customer message posted: short summary + mitigation steps + ETA for hardware triage. tenant-b replied acknowledging.
oncall-bot: oncall -> hardware-team handoff in 12m.
tay: run quick nvdiag and burn-in: `nvdiag --stress --duration 10m` started on node-04; results show ECC correctables keep increasing under synthetic load.
ricardo: hardware-team, can you confirm next steps?
hw-team: confirmed, escalate to board-level replacement. We'll pull the GPU and RMA. Recommend not returning node to prod until board validated.
ava: creating post-incident tasks: 1) add automated rule: if Xid_count > 4 in 10m, auto-cordon and route-shift; 2) add telemetry alert correlating kvcache growth + ECC spikes; 3) update runbook to prefer incremental drain.
emily: capturing customer impact for postmortem: tenant-b experienced ~14% error rate (9m window) and p95 latency increased 2.4x for 6m. No evidence of data corruption.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-058 status: mitigated -> monitoring.
ricardo: note for follow-up: investigate possible recent firmware upgrade on GPU images; cross-check with firmware changelog; we had similar pattern after 530.x driver rollout earlier.
hw-team: will log bench results and RMA details in HT-8892 and report back.
tay: adding runbook tweak: prefer `evictionGracePeriod=90` on serving pods to allow kvcache flush.
a va: typo in workflow noted, fixing doc.
emily: once replacement is scheduled, we will coordinate maintenance window and communicate ETA to affected customers.
ricardo: closing handoff to hw-team. posting handoff summary to infra-oncall.channel.
oncall-bot: Handoff complete: oncall -> hardware-team.
hw-team: bench logs: under heavy mem/stress, ECC correctables ramp and driver resets reproducible -> replacement approved.
ava: ordering replacement and scheduling removal from rack. will reopen thread after node reimage/test. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
